title_en: New Slang, New Stories (14/20): The Show-Off at the School Talent Show
note_en: In 动作浮夸得全场笑到直不起腰, the particle 得 after an adjective introduces how far something goes: "his moves were so over the top that the whole audience laughed until they couldn't stand up straight." English needs "so... that...", but Chinese just puts 得 between the description and its result.

sentences.en: He added that the word actually wasn't very nice at first; it meant someone who loves to grab attention and makes a fool of himself. But gradually, netizens started using it to praise people who dare to show themselves off and are bursting with personality, and it turned into an affectionate compliment.
